positions.name: AsyncJobContractRatifiedAsSettled
positions.frame: Is the async job contract's shape (receipt-then-poll, no-blocking/no-loss guarantee, dispatch-then-poll-or-piggyback) being reported as a concluded, ratified decision rather than a design still under argument?
positions.why: All three expressions come from the same speaker describing the same contract in a single breath: src-1 performs the ratification and states the receipt/cursor mechanic, src-2 states the guarantees as flat settled facts (no hedging), and src-3 explicitly labels the dispatch pattern a 'Key decision.' The conviction reading marks all three as 'decision' register — stated as concluded, not advanced as a position being argued for — which is what makes them cohere as one directional group rather than three independent facts. The tension the frame holds: src-2's conditional ('if the client drops the receipt') is the one hypothetical note inside an otherwise fully realis, settled description — held here as part of the same ratified-settledness read rather than resolved away.
